questions.text: The opportunity cost of a student choosing to attend university instead of taking a job paying ₦500,000 a year is
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is the value of the best alternative forgone — here the salary the student gives up by choosing university.

questions.text: A consumer is willing to pay ₦500 for a good but actually pays ₦350. The consumer surplus is
questions.explanation: Consumer surplus = amount willing to pay − amount actually paid = 500 − 350 = ₦150.

questions.text: Points lying outside a production possibility frontier are
options: unattainable with the available resources and technology
questions.explanation: The PPF shows maximum attainable combinations; points beyond it cannot be reached unless resources or technology increase.

questions.text: A fall in the cost of production will shift the supply curve to the
questions.explanation: Lower costs make producers willing to supply more at each price, shifting the supply curve rightwards. Higher costs shift it left.

questions.topic: Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis
questions.text: The range of the data set 5, 9, 14, 20 and 27 is
questions.explanation: Range = highest value − lowest value = 27 − 5 = 22.

questions.text: Positive economics is concerned with
options: statements about what ought to be
statements about what is, based on facts
questions.explanation: Positive statements are testable descriptions of economic reality. Normative statements express value judgements about what ought to be.

questions.topic: Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis
questions.text: The mean of the numbers 4, 6, 8, 10 and 12 is
A firm's total fixed cost is ₦200 and its total variable cost is ₦300 when it produces 50 units. Its average cost is
questions.explanation: Total cost = 200 + 300 = ₦500; average cost = 500 ÷ 50 = ₦10.

questions.topic: Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis
questions.text: The median of the set of numbers 3, 7, 9, 12, 15 and 18 is
questions.explanation: With six numbers, the median is the mean of the 3rd and 4th values: (9 + 12) ÷ 2 = 10.5.

questions.text: A maximum price fixed below the equilibrium price will result in
options: a rise in the market price
questions.explanation: At a price below equilibrium, quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied, creating a shortage (excess demand).

questions.text: The law of diminishing marginal utility states that as a consumer takes more units of a good, the additional satisfaction from each extra unit
questions.explanation: Each successive unit adds less extra satisfaction than the previous one, although total utility may still be rising.

questions.text: A minimum wage fixed above the equilibrium wage in a labour market is likely to cause
questions.explanation: At a wage above equilibrium, the supply of labour exceeds the demand for it, creating a surplus of labour — unemployment.

questions.text: When the price of a good falls from ₦20 to ₦16, the quantity demanded rises from 100 to 140 units. The price elasticity of demand is
questions.explanation: Percentage change in quantity = 40%; percentage change in price = 20%; elasticity = 40 ÷ 20 = 2, so demand is elastic.

questions.text: If a consumer's income rises by 10% and the quantity demanded of a good rises by 5%, the income elasticity of demand is
questions.explanation: Income elasticity = percentage change in quantity ÷ percentage change in income = 5 ÷ 10 = 0.5, so the good is a normal necessity.

questions.text: An increase in the price of a substitute good will cause the demand for the good in question to
questions.explanation: Consumers switch away from the dearer substitute towards the good, so its demand rises at every price.

questions.text: Division of labour leads to higher productivity mainly because workers
questions.explanation: Specialisation lets each worker concentrate on one task, gaining skill and speed. Higher wages may follow, but they are not the cause of the productivity gain.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT included in the calculation of a country's gross domestic product?
questions.explanation: Transfer payments involve no current production of goods or services, so they are excluded from GDP to avoid double counting.

questions.text: Bulk purchasing of raw materials at lower prices is an example of
questions.explanation: Buying in bulk is a marketing (commercial) economy of large-scale production. Technical economies come from better machinery and financial economies from cheaper borrowing.

questions.text: Given the demand function Qd = 100 − 2P and the supply function Qs = 20 + 2P, the equilibrium price is
questions.explanation: At equilibrium Qd = Qs: 100 − 2P = 20 + 2P, so 4P = 80 and P = ₦20.

questions.text: If the cash reserve ratio is 20%, the money multiplier is
questions.explanation: Money multiplier = 1 ÷ reserve ratio = 1 ÷ 0.2 = 5.

questions.text: The total utility derived from consuming successive units of a good is 10, 18, 24 and 28 utils. The marginal utility of the third unit is
questions.explanation: Marginal utility = change in total utility = 24 − 18 = 6 utils.

questions.text: A firm sells 40 units of a product at ₦25 each. Its total revenue is
questions.explanation: Total revenue = price × quantity = 25 × 40 = ₦1,000.

questions.text: Under a tax system in which the first ₦100,000 of income is taxed at 5% and the rest at 10%, the tax payable on an income of ₦300,000 is
Money performs the function of a store of value when it
questions.explanation: As a store of value, money holds its worth so it can be saved and spent later. Buying goods is the medium-of-exchange function and measuring prices is the unit-of-account function.

questions.text: When the marginal product of labour is zero, the total product is
questions.explanation: Total product rises while marginal product is positive and is greatest at the point where marginal product reaches zero; beyond that, total product falls.

questions.text: A tax system in which higher incomes are taxed at a higher proportion of income is described as
questions.explanation: A progressive tax takes a larger percentage from higher incomes. A regressive tax takes a larger percentage from lower incomes, and a proportional tax takes the same percentage from all.

questions.text: If GNP is ₦900 billion and depreciation (capital consumption) is ₦100 billion, the net national product is
questions.explanation: NNP = GNP − depreciation = 900 − 100 = ₦800 billion.

questions.text: The Central Bank of Nigeria controls the money supply through all of the following EXCEPT
questions.explanation: Open market operations, reserve requirements and the bank rate are monetary policy tools. Income tax is a fiscal tool of government, not the central bank.

questions.text: If the exchange rate is ₦1,500 to $1, the naira cost of goods valued at $200 is
Which of the following is a function of a commercial bank?
options: Acting as lender of last resort
questions.explanation: Commercial banks take deposits and lend to customers. Issuing currency, controlling money supply and acting as lender of last resort are central bank functions.

questions.text: If a country's GDP is ₦800 billion and its net factor income from abroad is ₦50 billion, its GNP is
questions.explanation: GNP = GDP + net factor income from abroad = 800 + 50 = ₦850 billion.

questions.text: If the price of a good rises by 20% and the quantity supplied rises by 30%, the price elasticity of supply is
questions.explanation: Elasticity of supply = 30 ÷ 20 = 1.5, so supply is elastic.

questions.text: Demand-pull inflation is caused by
options: excess aggregate demand over available supply
an increase in the money supply only
questions.explanation: When total spending outruns the economy's capacity to produce, prices are pulled up. Cost-push inflation, by contrast, comes from rising costs.

questions.text: A general and persistent fall in the prices of goods and services is known as
questions.explanation: Deflation is falling prices. Inflation is rising prices, stagflation combines inflation with stagnation, and disinflation is a slowing rate of inflation.

questions.text: Product differentiation is a distinguishing feature of
questions.explanation: In monopolistic competition many firms sell similar but differentiated products, using branding and advertising. Perfect competitors sell identical products.

questions.text: Government spending on the construction of roads and hospitals is classified as
questions.explanation: Capital expenditure buys durable assets. Recurrent expenditure covers day-to-day running costs such as salaries, and transfer payments involve no goods in return.

questions.text: If the consumer price index rises from 120 to 150, the rate of inflation is
Economic development differs from economic growth mainly because development includes
options: improvements in living standards and welfare
a rise in real GDP only
questions.explanation: Growth is a rise in output; development adds better health, education, equality and quality of life to the increase in output.

questions.text: The kinked demand curve model is used to explain price rigidity in
questions.explanation: In an oligopoly, rivals match price cuts but not price rises, producing a kink at the ruling price and making prices sticky.

questions.text: A public limited company differs from a private limited company mainly because it can
options: be owned by one person only
offer its shares for sale to the general public
operate without a board of directors
questions.explanation: A public limited company may invite the public to subscribe to its shares, while a private limited company may not.

questions.text: A firm that processes raw materials into finished goods belongs to the
questions.explanation: The secondary sector covers manufacturing and processing. The primary sector extracts raw materials and the tertiary sector provides services.

questions.text: The labour force of a country consists of
options: the employed plus the unemployed who are willing and able to work
questions.explanation: The labour force includes everyone of working age who is working or actively seeking work; children, retirees and those not seeking work are excluded.

questions.text: In a perfectly competitive market, an individual firm is a
questions.explanation: Each firm is too small to influence the market price, so it accepts the price set by the forces of demand and supply.

questions.text: The reward for the factor of production known as entrepreneurship is
questions.explanation: The entrepreneur bears risk and organises production, receiving profit. Land earns rent, labour earns wages and capital earns interest.

questions.text: A budget deficit occurs when government
questions.explanation: A deficit means spending more than is collected in a period; the gap is financed by borrowing. Revenue above spending is a surplus.

questions.text: A country's balance of trade is in surplus when its
questions.explanation: The balance of trade covers visible goods only; a surplus means exports of goods exceed imports of goods.

questions.text: The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) was established primarily to promote
options: economic integration among West African states
political union of West African states
questions.explanation: ECOWAS, founded by the Treaty of Lagos in 1975, aims at economic cooperation and integration, including free movement of goods and people.

questions.text: A country is said to have a comparative advantage in producing a good when it can produce the good
options: at a lower opportunity cost than other countries
using fewer resources than other countries
questions.explanation: Comparative advantage depends on relative opportunity cost, not on using fewer resources, which is absolute advantage.

questions.text: In a mixed economy, resources are allocated by
options: both the price mechanism and the government
questions.explanation: A mixed economy combines market forces with government intervention to correct market failures and provide public goods.

questions.text: A country with a population of 200 million growing at 2.5% per year adds how many people per year?
questions.explanation: Annual increase = 2.5% × 200 million = 5 million people.

questions.text: Subsistence farming is characterised mainly by
questions.explanation: Subsistence farmers grow food chiefly to feed their own households, using simple tools and family labour.

questions.text: Seasonal unemployment occurs mainly in
questions.explanation: Work in farming and tourism varies with the seasons, so workers are idle out of season. Banking, the civil service and manufacturing employ workers more steadily.

questions.text: The reward for land as a factor of production is
questions.explanation: Land earns rent, labour earns wages, capital earns interest and entrepreneurship earns profit.

questions.text: Joint supply occurs when two goods
options: are produced together from the same process
questions.explanation: Joint supply means goods come from one process, e.g. petrol and kerosene from crude oil. Goods used together are in joint demand, and goods competing for resources are in competitive supply.

questions.text: A tax imposed on imported goods is known as a
questions.explanation: A tariff is a duty charged on imports. A quota limits quantity, a subsidy supports producers, and an embargo bans trade altogether.

questions.text: OPEC is an organisation of countries that are major exporters of
questions.explanation: The Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries coordinates petroleum policies among its member states, including Nigeria.

questions.text: If the naira depreciates against the dollar, imported goods in Nigeria will become
questions.explanation: Depreciation means more naira are needed to buy each dollar, so the naira price of imports rises.

questions.text: The economic problem of what to produce is solved in a free enterprise economy mainly by
questions.explanation: In a market economy, consumer demand and prices signal what firms should produce. Central planning and tradition solve the problem in other systems.

questions.text: A good whose demand falls as consumers' incomes rise is called
questions.explanation: Inferior goods, such as low-quality staples, are bought less as incomes rise and consumers switch to better alternatives.

questions.text: Which of the following is an obstacle to economic development in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Heavy reliance on one export makes the economy vulnerable to oil price shocks. A large population and natural resources are potential assets, not obstacles in themselves.
